configs.what: Trent, the AI Security Engineer with its documented defaults.
Security connectors (Semgrep, Snyk, Sonar, SARIF) and team connectors (Jira, Linear, Slack, Notion) that the customer connects.
Trent connected to the customer's coding agent through the Trent plugin or the remote MCP server.
The fully automatic remediation loop, run only on finding categories the team has confirmed once.

facts.label: It executes actions itself
facts.fact: Through the team connectors the llm-info page lists (Jira, Linear, Slack, Notion), Trent raises remediation tickets in Linear or Jira; the page calls this path Manual because people then make the fix.
facts.quote: Trent raises a ticket in Linear or Jira with exact remediation instructions.

facts.label: The agent handles routine tasks; the person is consulted on exceptions
facts.fact: In the fully automatic path Trent confirms a category of finding with the team once, then hands such findings to the coding agent and verifies the fix; findings that need a person come to the team with a recommended decision.
facts.quote: The findings that need human attention, Trent brings to you proactively

facts.label: It asks for narrower access than the whole account
facts.fact: Trent's plugin README says Trent reads a repository through the Trent GitHub App installed on that repository and the plugin sends only the repository's owner and name, and Trent's agent-native product post lists installing GitHub apps among the actions kept in Trent's dashboard.
facts.quote: Trent reads a repository through the Trent GitHub App you install on it.

facts.label: High-impact actions need a person's approval
facts.fact: Deleting projects, managing keys, inviting members and installing GitHub apps are left to a person in the dashboard.
facts.quote: Those decisions stay with the human who accepts their consequences.

facts.label: Test or evaluation results are published
facts.fact: Trent publishes benchmark results on 28 CWE-Bench CVEs against other tools, with method and run counts.
facts.quote: Trent detected 33–47% of 43 labelled vulnerability instances in 28 CVEs

facts.label: There is a channel to report problems with it or contest its output
facts.fact: Users can contest a finding's severity and correct requirements; corrections are recorded.
facts.quote: You can challenge a severity and apply a regrade in place

facts.label: It is machine-readable for agents: it publishes an llms.txt, an AGENTS.md, an API description or an agent card
facts.fact: An llms.txt resolves at the site root and maps product, research and company pages.
facts.quote: This file is a map of Trent AI

help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Trent AI's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
